name: Erlang
title: Erlang (OTP 29)

type.text: **Dynamic typing**: A value carries its type at run time, so a type fault appears when the expression executes
**No declared parameter or return types**: `-spec` is optional metadata, and the language has no generic type parameters
**No sum types**: A tagged tuple such as `{ok, Value}` or `{error, Reason}` is a convention, and no type checks the union
**Dispatch is checked at run time**: `Mod:Fun(Args)` resolves when called, so a missing function fails there rather than at compile time
**`-spec` and Dialyzer give optional static analysis**: A success-typing pass over the compiled BEAM files detects inconsistent calls
**Atoms serve as named constants**: An atom such as `ok`, `error`, or `undefined` is a distinct value, so the language needs no null

construction.text: **All data is immutable**: A term cannot be changed after it is built
**A pattern in the clause head selects the construction path**: The arguments decide which clause runs
**Records and maps declare named structure**: `-record(user, {name, age})` gives compile-time named fields over a tuple
**State is a value threaded through recursion**: An OTP behaviour receives its state and returns the new state, so no object owns it
**A process is the unit of mutable state**: A `gen_server` owns its state and exposes it by message
**A record is a tuple**: Field access is positional at run time, so the record definition must be shared by every module that uses it

memory.text: **Collection is per-process and non-deterministic**: A process collects its own heap on its own schedule
**A private heap confines a pause**: A collection affects one process, and there is no global stop-the-world pause
**No manual deallocation**: The VM reclaims memory, and a program never frees a term
**Off-heap binaries are reference counted**: A binary above the heap threshold is shared between processes rather than copied
**A large live set costs more per collection**: A process that accumulates state pays a higher collection cost
**An ETS table lives outside the collector**: The table persists until its owner deletes it or dies

error.text: **Exceptions are unchecked**: `throw`, `error`, and `exit` are not declared, so a caller cannot see the failure set from a signature
**"Let it crash" makes failure a supervision event**: A supervisor restarts a failed process, and the normal path carries no recovery code
**Links and monitors define propagation**: `link/1` couples the fates of two processes, and `monitor/2` reports a failure without dying
**A pattern-match failure raises a defined error**: An unmatched value raises `badmatch`, and an unmatched clause raises `function_clause`
**`try`/`catch`/`after` is available when recovery is local**: A `catch` clause separates `throw`, `error`, and `exit`
**A restart resets process state**: Supervision restores the process, not the data it held, so state must be recoverable

concurrency.text: **The actor model is the core of the language**: Processes share no memory and communicate by message
**`spawn`, `link`, and `monitor` are primitives**: Starting and observing a process needs no library
**The BEAM schedules preemptively by reductions**: A process cannot hold a scheduler indefinitely
**Messages are immutable values**: A message is copied or shared by reference count, never aliased mutably
**Distribution is built into the VM**: `net_kernel` and `epmd` let a process send to a node as if it were local
**Distribution is designed, not automatic**: Node failure, network partition, and message loss must be handled by the application

platform.text: **The BEAM is portable and open source**: The Erlang runtime runs on Linux, macOS, Windows, and BSD
**Hot code loading is a runtime feature**: `code:load_file/1` replaces a module while the system runs
**A release bundles the runtime and the application**: `release_handler` and `reltool` produce a deployable node
**Distribution across nodes is a platform feature**: Nodes discover each other and pass messages without an external broker
**The runtime must be present**: An Erlang program runs on the VM, so the artefact is not a native binary on its own
**Poor fit for CPU-bound numerical work**: The VM is not built for dense numeric computation, so that work belongs in another language

performance.text: **The BEAM handles very many concurrent I/O processes**: A process is cheap and needs no thread
**BeamAsm compiles hot code**: The JIT added in OTP 24 means bytecode is not always interpreted
**Per-process collection avoids a global pause**: A collection affects one process
**Reduction scheduling bounds latency**: A process yields after a fixed number of reductions
**CPU-bound computation is weak relative to native code**: A tight numeric loop trails C or Rust
**A NIF runs on a scheduler thread**: A native function that runs long blocks other processes on that scheduler

ecosystem.text: **Hex.pm and `rebar3` cover packages and builds**: A registry, dependency resolution, and release builds are all present
**OTP ships with the language**: Supervision, `gen_server`, `application`, and release handling are part of the distribution
**Elixir libraries are reachable through interop**: The two languages run on one VM and call each other directly
**The flagship projects are long-lived and battle-tested**: RabbitMQ, CouchDB, Riak, and WhatsApp's messaging stack are Erlang systems
**OTP is documented as a first-class topic**: The OTP design principles document the behaviours
**The library count is smaller than the mainstream**: Fewer general-purpose packages exist outside messaging and telecom
The NIF ABI is versioned and checked at load, and an older major is accepted for two releases [@erlNif]

**Stored terms cross on a published promise**: the external term format carries its version, and Erlang/OTP systems as of R16B decode the minor-version-2 encoding that is the default as of OTP 26.0 [@erlangErlang]

evolution.text: **The language has kept backward compatibility for decades**: Code written against an old OTP release continues to run
**Hot code loading decouples deployment from runtime**: A module is replaced while the system runs
**`code_change/3` migrates state across a version change**: An OTP behaviour converts old state to the new shape
**OTP release handling gives a controlled upgrade path**: `release_handler` applies a version change to a running node
**A hot upgrade must be designed**: State migration and dependency order are the application's responsibility

domain.text: **Excellent fit for distributed, fault-tolerant systems**: Supervision, distribution, and the actor model match the problem directly
**Proven in telecom and messaging**: WhatsApp, RabbitMQ, and Discord's infrastructure run on the BEAM
**Binary parsing is a strength**: The bit syntax `<<A:8, B:16/little>>` matches a protocol frame directly
**Distribution across nodes requires explicit design effort**: The application must decide how to handle a lost node

learning.text: **The learning curve is steep**: A developer learns functional programming, the actor model, and OTP at once
**The Prolog-derived syntax is unfamiliar**: The `.`, `,`, and `;` delimiters and the term syntax differ from the mainstream
**The surface is large**: The language, the OTP behaviours, and the VM's semantics are separate bodies of knowledge
**The official documentation is thorough**: The Erlang reference manual and the OTP design principles are authoritative
**The community is established**: Decades of accumulated material and answered questions exist

syntax.text: **The term syntax is uniform**: Every construct is a term, and a module is a sequence of forms ending in a period
**The delimiter roles are consistent**: A comma separates expressions, a semicolon separates clauses, and a period ends a form
**Bit syntax is compact for protocols**: A binary pattern states field widths and endianness in one expression
**Pattern matching is part of the function-head syntax**: A clause states its cases directly
**The comma, semicolon, and period distinction is easy to get wrong**: One misplaced delimiter changes the meaning of a form
**Atoms and variables differ only by case**: `ok` is an atom and `Ok` is a variable

testing.text: **EUnit and Common Test ship with OTP**: Unit tests and system tests are part of the standard distribution
**Property-based testing is available**: PropEr and QuickCheck generate inputs from a property
**Tracing and `observer` inspect a running system**: `dbg`, `recon`, and the observer tool expose processes, messages, and scheduler load
**Common Test runs a distributed suite**: A test can start several nodes and drive them together
**Errors surface at run time**: Dynamic typing defers a type fault to the executed path
**Dialyzer catches some faults and not all**: Success typing proves the absence of some inconsistencies, not the presence of correctness

security.text: **Process isolation contains a fault**: A crashed process does not corrupt another process's memory
**Messages are immutable values**: No shared mutable state exists to race on
**The supervision tree bounds a failure**: A restarted process returns the system to a known state
**The atom table has a fixed limit**: `list_to_atom/1` or `binary_to_atom/2` on untrusted input can exhaust the table, whose default ceiling is about one million atoms
**`binary_to_term/1` on untrusted input is dangerous**: Decoding an external term can allocate a large structure unless the `safe` option is used
**A NIF and a `Port` reach unsafe code**: Native code can break the VM's guarantees

tradeoffs: **The syntax is Prolog-derived**: The form is unfamiliar to most developers; this is a learning property, not a coupling
**Distribution is a design task**: The language supplies the transport, and the application decides the failure semantics
**Weak CPU-bound performance is a domain fit note**: The VM is built for I/O concurrency, not for numeric loops
**Hot upgrade constrains state handling**: The running system can change module code, so the application must supply a `code_change/3` callback to migrate state
**Atoms are named constants in place of null**: Absence is carried by an atom convention such as `undefined`
**Records are tuples by design**: The representation is a deliberate choice made for compactness and speed
verdict: Erlang's design yields moderate language-imposed coupling in the domain it was built for. The actor model removes shared memory from concurrency, immutability removes in-place mutation, and "let it crash" with OTP supervision moves recovery out of the business logic. Main strengths: processes are cheap and isolated, the BEAM schedules preemptively, per-process collection avoids a global pause, and hot code loading decouples deployment from runtime. Main weaknesses: the language is dynamically typed, so a type fault surfaces at run time; exceptions are unchecked; the syntax is unfamiliar; and distribution across nodes must be designed rather than assumed.

energy.text: Runs on a virtual machine, above native code in the energy and time benchmarks [@pereira2017energy]; a causal re-analysis attributes most of the gap to execution time [@vankempen2025green].

ai-readiness.text: Sparse training data: models write it unreliably [@joel2025lowresource].

safety.text: No certified or standards-qualified path for safety-critical systems.

delivery.note: A hex package ships source the release compiles
The NIF API version compiles into the library, and the runtime checks it at load

data_formats.note: Erlang encodes stored terms in the external term format, carries the version in the encoding, and publishes the reading promise: Erlang/OTP systems as of R16B decode the minor-version-2 encoding that is the default as of OTP 26.0
